subject: Post-call: Vertex usage buckets & preliminary pricing worksheet
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@vertexinc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Vertex usage buckets & preliminary pricing worksheet

Hi Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap + next steps from our discovery: 

1) Agreed usage buckets (monthly token estimate):
   - Search/metadata indexing (short queries): ~10M tokens/mo
   - Chat interactions (avg 300 tokens per conv): 4M convs/mo → ~1.2B tokens/mo
   - Batch embeddings (nightly jobs): ~50M tokens/mo
   - Peak burst days expected: ~20% above average for 3–5 days/month

2) Budget signals you shared: target run-rate between $20k–$50k/month for initial rollout. You mentioned a desired target unit cost of ~$400–$800 per 1M tokens depending on SLA/latency.

3) Items I promised: preliminary pricing worksheet with 3 scenarios (Metered hosted, Committed Dedicated (6/12mo), and Hybrid with KV cache & batching assumptions). See attached "vertex_usage_buckets.xlsx" and a CSV that powers the cost lines.

Quick notes on assumptions (explained in the worksheet):
- Baseline model: open-model LlamaX-16B (quantized) — baseline compute cost assigned for hosted path.
- Caching factor: we modeled a conservative 1.6x effective token reduction for repeated prefixes (applies primarily to chat).
- Batching/throughput: we include a 20% token cost reduction for deduped batch windows on nightly jobs.
- Discount tiers: 10% at $100k/mo commit, 18% at $250k/mo, with negotiated caps for enterprise SLAs.

Requested confirmation from you: could you confirm the monthly token buckets above (rough order-of-magnitude is OK) and whether procurement prefers a committed-commit or metered month-to-month pilot?

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm buckets + target $/1M token figure you want me to use for the formal invoice estimate (I used $600/1M as a midpoint in the worksheet).
- I’ll circulate an "invoice estimate" PDF and a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) we can use with Procurement.
- Schedule a short follow-up (20 min) next week to walk the worksheet.

Attachments: vertex_usage_buckets.xlsx, redwood_pricing_scenarios.csv

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Mobile: +1 555-210-9987

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@vertexinc.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@vertexinc.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 17:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Vertex usage buckets & preliminary pricing worksheet

Thanks Neha — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Buckets look roughly right. The chat estimate is the one we’ll validate with product usage logs — give us a day to confirm.
- Procurement preference: we prefer a 3-month committed pilot if you can provide a capped commit + burn rate; otherwise a metered pilot is OK but harder for forecasting.
- The $20k–$50k/mo is our current budget window for a pilot; long-term commit depends on a further 3x–5x uplift in user engagement.

Requests for the formal estimate: 
- Can you show both: (A) Hosted metered price per 1M tokens, (B) Dedicated 6-mo commit effective price per 1M tokens (including any KV/cache impacts), and (C) A blended line showing effective $/1M for our mid-case volumes?
- Please include an explicit line for SLA (99.9% vs 99.95%) cost delta if you have it.

Timing: procurement wants an "invoice estimate" they can attach to the internal request by Tue 10 Mar. Can you hit that?

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Head of Product Integrations, Vertex Inc
alex.chen@vertexinc.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@vertexinc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Vertex usage buckets & preliminary pricing worksheet

Alex — thanks, yes we can deliver the three-line estimate you asked for and include SLA deltas. I attached a compact "invoice_estimate_VTX-2026-045.pdf" that pulls numbers from the attached spreadsheet and shows three scenarios side-by-side. Summary highlights from the estimate (all numbers are example-effective $/1M tokens):

Scenario A — Metered Hosted (no commit)
- Model: LlamaX-16B (quant)
- Effective $/1M tokens: $780
- Notes: higher per-token but flexible, 24/7 hosted support, no commit

Scenario B — Dedicated (6-mo commit, $120k/mo)
- Provisioned capacity with reserved GPU pools
- Effective $/1M tokens: $430 (includes baseline 12% commit discount + batching/KV assumptions)
- Notes: predictable throughput, lower p99 latency, requires contract + payment terms

Scenario C — Hybrid (metered with KV cache & batching credits)
- Blended effective $/1M tokens: $560
- Notes: Lower TCO if chat skew and caching realises; good mid-pilot option

Assumptions called out in the PDF:
- Token mix: 70% chat, 25% embeddings, 5% admin queries.
- Cache realization: 1.6x token reduction for repeated prefixes (chat) applied to effective cost line.
- Batching credit: 20% on scheduled batch jobs.
- Discounting: finance-approved up to 12% for $120k/mo commit; larger discounts require sales approval.

I’ve CC’d Rishi (finance) and Marissa (sales lead) to confirm the discount guardrails and to get a formal sign-off if we want to push beyond the 12% baseline. If this looks good I’ll: 
- Finalize the PDF with a one-page MAP and send a HubSpot deal update (link included).
- Propose a quick 20-min call Mon 9 Mar to walk through the worksheet with Procurement.

Attachments: invoice_estimate_VTX-2026-045.pdf, vertex_usage_buckets.xlsx, redwood_pricing_scenarios.csv

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

> > Hi Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap + next steps from our discovery...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Vertex usage buckets & preliminary pricing worksheet

Neha — reviewed the numbers. A couple of quick points from my side: 

- Finance (Rishi) approved the 12% discount band at $120k/mo commit; any request to go to ~18% (or larger) requires a short business case (customers want to see a >6mo payback or a ref in their vertical).
- Approve sending the PDF estimate to Procurement and suggest we include a 30-day pilot clause for the committed option. That makes it easier to move forward and keeps legal exposure low.

Rishi — can you confirm the billing cadence we should propose (monthly invoice vs upfront quarterly) and whether we need PO language for a 3-month pilot?

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
